entries.title: Extreme Close-Up (ECU)
entries.text:
Extreme Close-Up (ECU)

ECUItalian shotchokerdetail close-upFacial detailTrès gros plan

An extreme close-up, or extreme close up shot, fills the frame with one small feature: an eye, a mouth, a fingertip, a trigger. Surrounding space disappears; the crop is tighter than a whole face.

Volume

Create this Extreme Close-Up

Narrative function

Size is a sentence. An extreme close-up says the scene is this fragment: a pupil tightening, a lip splitting, a safety clicking off.

Cutting between such fragments can turn looking into a physical confrontation, as in a standoff built from eyes instead of bodies. It is the wrong tool when the actor still needs a whole face to play the line.

If you can still see hairline and chin together, you have not arrived at this size. Use it when a detail is the event, then get out before the texture becomes a poster.

How it works

Pick the anatomical landmark that hits the frame lines. Camera distance and focal length are separate from the crop: a 75mm or 100mm a few feet back keeps facial proportion; a wide lens inches from the skin balloons the nose.

A macro is only required when the feature is truly small, such as an iris or a watch gear. Tight framing, macro optics, and shallow depth of field are three different choices.

Light a small source if you want pore and scar; wrap if you want the fragment to stay readable. Prompt the exact feature and the crop (brow to upper cheek, mouth only), not a vague tight close-up.

When to use it

Use it when a detail is the scene: the eye that decides to fire, the mouth that will not speak. Do not use it as a default portrait or for ordinary dialogue; the rest of the person is information you have thrown away.

Compared with similar shots

A Choker Shot still holds a whole face from hairline to chin. A Close-Up keeps head and upper shoulders.

An extreme close-up is a fragment, not a portrait. An Insert Shot can be this tight, but an insert is a story object or hand fact, not a size.

If the frame still includes both eyes and a mouth as a face, you are not here yet.

Choker ShotEmotion with nowhere to hide.

Close-UpRead micro-expression. Default for important dialogue.

Insert ShotPoint at the thing that will matter later.

In film

In The Good, the Bad and the Ugly, eyes and faces dominate the final standoff montage until looking becomes the gunfight. The Passion of Joan of Arc puts interrogation pressure on facial fragments.

Persona uses faces so close that identity starts to fuse. Borrow the grammar of fragment versus whole, not a poster of an iris.

The Good, the Bad and the Ugly 1966Eyes and faces dominate the final standoff montage.

The Passion of Joan of Arc 1928Faces carry the pressure of the interrogation and trial.

Prompt it

Lead with the crop, then the feature. Example: Extreme close-up of [Subject], a single feature filling the frame, pores and texture, tighter than forehead-to-chin.

Name which feature (left eye, mouth, fingertip, trigger) and what must stay sharp. Do not write tight close-up, choker, or macro unless you actually need those.

For video, lock the camera, keep the feature in frame, and allow only a blink, a swallow, or a tiny gaze shift.

Use in Video Generator

Extreme close-up of an older watchmaker’s eyes as she decides whether to open a sealed mechanism. Frame from brow to upper cheek, natural skin texture, tiny shift in gaze and controlled breathing. Restrained light, stable focus, no cosmetic smoothing or wide-angle facial distortion.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Choker Shot or a Close-Up: the whole face still reads. The tell is hairline and chin both present, or shoulders sneaking in.

The other tell is wide-angle distortion from parking a short lens on the nose. Fix: name the feature, crop inside the face, and pick a longer lens or a true macro only if the object is small.

Questions

What is Extreme Close-Up in film?

An extreme close-up is a shot size that fills the frame with one small feature such as an eye, a mouth, or a fingertip. It is tighter than a whole-face crop, so surrounding space becomes secondary or disappears.

Extreme Close-Up vs Choker Shot

A choker still shows a complete face from hairline to chin. An extreme close-up is a fragment: one feature, not the whole portrait. If both eyes and the mouth read as a face, you are in choker or close-up territory.

When should I use Extreme Close-Up?

Use it when the detail is the event: a trigger, an eye, a cracked lip. Skip it for ordinary talk, beauty portraits, or any beat that still needs the rest of the head and shoulders.

How do I prompt Extreme Close-Up for AI image or video?

Write Extreme close-up of [Subject], name the single feature, and say it fills the frame tighter than forehead-to-chin. Add pores and texture if you need skin fact. For video, lock off and allow only a tiny motion in that feature.

entries.title: Choker Shot (BCU)
entries.text:
Choker Shot (BCU)

Big Close-UpBig Close UpBCU

A choker shot, also called a big close-up (BCU), frames the face from hairline to chin, often clipping the skull on every side. Shoulders are out; almost no background remains.

Create this Choker Shot

Narrative function

A choker traps a person in their own face. There is nowhere to gesture, no collar to hide in, no room tone in the corners.

Emotion has to happen in the eyes, the mouth, and the tiny muscles around them. It is the wrong tool when you still need a swallow, a shoulder, or a hand at the chest.

It is also the wrong tool if you only wanted pores on one feature: that job belongs to a tighter fragment. Hold a choker when the scene is a confession, a breakdown, or a stare with no escape, then cut out before the crop feels like a passport photo.

How it works

Put the top frame at the hairline and the bottom at the chin. Ears often clip.

Headroom is nearly zero. A 75mm to 100mm from portrait distance keeps the face from ballooning; a wide lens this close will warp the skull.

Camera at Eye Level unless you want a power tilt. Focus the nearer eye.

Light can be hard enough to show sweat, or wrapped if the performance is the only contrast. Prompt: Choker shot of [Subject] from hairline to chin, almost no background.

When to use it

Use it when emotion has nowhere to hide: a whispered admission, a stare across a table that has become a cell. Do not use it if you still need upper body language, or if the story is actually one feature (an eye, a mouth) rather than the whole face.

Compared with similar shots

An Extreme Close-Up is tighter than the face: one feature, not hairline-to-chin. A Close-Up includes the upper shoulders and a little air around the head.

A choker, also called a big close-up or BCU, is the in-between prison: a complete face with no body. Do not treat BCU and ECU as synonyms.

Extreme Close-UpA detail is the scene: an eye, a mouth, a trigger.

Close-UpRead micro-expression. Default for important dialogue.

Medium Close-UpTalk without losing body language.

In film

Persona pushes faces until they occupy the whole rectangle and start to trade identity. Black Swan uses this proximity when the performance has no backstage left.

Use those as grammar for pressure, not as a look-alike brief.

Prompt it

Quote the crop. Example: Choker shot of [Subject] from hairline to chin, almost no background.

Add lens only if you need undistorted proportion (75mm to 100mm). Do not write extreme close-up, and do not ask for shoulders.

For video, lock the head in that crop; a lean that reveals clavicle has left the size.

Use in Image Generator

Choker shot of [Subject] from hairline to chin, almost no background, claustrophobic portrait, Bergman proximity.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is an Extreme Close-Up (only an eye) or a Close-Up (shoulders still in). The tell is either a fragment with no chin, or a collar and headroom.

Fix: hairline and chin are the frame lines; nothing below the jaw.

Questions

What is Choker Shot in film?

A choker shot, also called a big close-up (BCU), is a very tight face crop, usually from hairline to chin, with almost no background and no shoulders. It is not an extreme close-up of a single feature.

Choker Shot vs Close-Up

A close-up holds the head and upper shoulders, so a little body and air remain. A choker cuts at the chin and hairline, so the face is the entire subject. If you can still see clavicle or coat collar, you are in close-up, not choker.

When should I use Choker Shot?

Use it when a face has nowhere to hide: confession, panic, a stare that is the scene. Do not use it for ordinary dialogue, and do not use it when the story is one feature rather than the whole face.

How do I prompt Choker Shot for AI image or video?

Write Choker shot of [Subject] from hairline to chin, almost no background. Forbid shoulders. For video, keep that crop locked so a nod does not introduce chest or sky.

entries.title: Close-Up (CU)
entries.text:
Close-Up (CU)

CU

A close-up, or close up shot, frames a face tightly enough to privilege detail over surroundings, usually head and upper shoulders. The room becomes secondary; the person still reads as a head, not a fragment.

Create this Close-Up

Narrative function

A close-up is a new fact on a face. It is the default for important dialogue because micro-expression, a lie, or a decision can be read without losing the idea of a person.

The shoulders keep a little body in the sentence so a swallow or a turned collar still exists. It is the wrong tool when the beat is a hand, a holster, or the door across the room.

It is also the wrong tool as a beauty setting on every line: if you live here, coverage becomes a slideshow of heads. Change size when the new scale reveals a fact this crop cannot prove.

How it works

Bottom frame at the upper chest or clavicle; top just above the hair, with modest Headroom. A 65mm to 85mm at conversation distance is common; the catalog 75mm Cooke is a portrait working length, not a requirement.

Shallow Focus will drop the room, but the size is the crop, not the bokeh. Match reverse size if this is dialogue.

Prompt: Tight close-up of [Subject], head and upper shoulders.

When to use it

Use it to read micro-expression on an important line: the moment a person decides not to answer. Do not use it as wallpaper on every sentence, and do not use it when the information is below the chest.

Compared with similar shots

A Choker Shot cuts off the shoulders and sits on hairline and chin. A Medium Close-Up starts at the chest and still shows dialogue-distance body language.

An Extreme Close-Up is a fragment inside the face. Close-up is the portrait size: head plus upper shoulders, not MCU, not choker, not ECU.

Medium Close-UpTalk without losing body language.

Choker ShotEmotion with nowhere to hide.

Extreme Close-UpA detail is the scene: an eye, a mouth, a trigger.

In film

The Passion of Joan of Arc builds trial pressure from faces that still read as heads, not only fragments. The Silence of the Lambs uses close-ups in the interviews so thought is visible while a little of the body remains.

Grammar: the face as the location, with enough shoulder to stay a person.

Prompt it

Name the anatomy. Example: Tight close-up of [Subject], head and upper shoulders, 75mm, shallow depth of field.

Do not write choker, chest up, or a single eye. Keep a sliver of collar or shoulder so the model does not crop inside the face.

For video, hold the head; a pull that reveals waist has become a different size.

Use in Image Generator

Tight close-up of [Subject], head and upper shoulders, shallow depth of field, creamy bokeh, 75mm Cooke, the face as landscape.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Medium Close-Up (too much chest and room) or a Choker Shot (no shoulders). The tell is either a talking-head with a lot of torso, or a face with no neck.

Fix: head and upper shoulders only. Another tell is calling any tight face a close-up when you meant ECU.

Questions

What is Close-Up in film?

A close-up is a shot that frames a face or object tightly enough that detail outranks the surroundings, typically head and upper shoulders. It is a size, not a mood, and it still shows a person rather than one isolated feature.

Close-Up vs Medium Close-Up

A medium close-up starts at the chest and keeps shoulders and some hand language readable at dialogue distance. A close-up is tighter: head and upper shoulders, with the room mostly gone. If you can still see mid-chest and a slice of set, you are in MCU.

When should I use Close-Up?

Use it when an important line or thought must be read on the face. Do not park every line here, and do not use it when the beat is a hand, a door, or a whole-face prison crop.

How do I prompt Close-Up for AI image or video?

Write Tight close-up of [Subject], head and upper shoulders. Add a 75mm if you want portrait proportion. For video, hold that crop; do not say close-up if you mean chest-up or hairline-to-chin.

entries.title: Medium Close-Up (MCU)
entries.text:
Medium Close-Up (MCU)

MCU

A medium close-up, or medium close up, usually frames a person from chest or shoulders upward. Dialogue distance remains: face, shoulders, and often a hand at chest height stay readable.

Create this Medium Close-Up

Narrative function

An MCU is how people talk when you still care about body language. You get the thought on the face and the small shrug, the glass raised, the cigarette, without dropping to the waist.

Most interview and table coverage lives here because the room is a slice, not a map. It is the wrong tool when the holster, the gait, or the architecture is the information.

It is also the wrong tool when the line needs a true close-up fact: an MCU will keep offering shoulders and wallpaper. Use it to talk; leave it when the scene stops being a conversation.

How it works

Bottom frame at mid-chest or the sternum. Hands can enter if they rise.

50mm to 75mm at sit-down distance is typical; the catalog 65 to 75mm is a working band, not a brand. You should still see a strip of set behind the shoulders.

Headroom is normal, not crushed. Prompt: Medium close-up of [Subject] from chest up, shoulders and hands still readable.

When to use it

Use it for dialogue that must keep body language: two people at a table, a phone call with a free hand. Do not use it when you need a waist-up gesture, a gunbelt, or a face with no chest left in frame.

Compared with similar shots

A Close-Up is head and upper shoulders, tighter than chest-up. A Medium Shot starts at the waist and balances gesture with face.

MCU is the band between them: chest up, talk without losing the shoulders. Do not write MCU when you mean CU, and do not call a waist shot a medium close-up.

Close-UpRead micro-expression. Default for important dialogue.

Medium ShotWorkhorse coverage. Most scenes live here.

Extreme Close-UpA detail is the scene: an eye, a mouth, a trigger.

In film

Heat uses this distance in the diner so two opponents can talk with shoulders and hands still in play before and between tighter singles. The Sopranos lives in MCU for talk that still needs a room sliver and a raised glass.

Grammar: conversation distance, not a beauty crop.

Prompt it

Say chest up. Example: Medium close-up of [Subject] from chest up, dialogue distance, shoulders and hands still readable, 65 to 75mm.

Do not say head and shoulders only, and do not say waist. For video, keep the chest line; a zoom into the eyes has become a close-up.

Use in Image Generator

Medium close-up of [Subject] from chest up, dialogue distance, shoulders and hands still readable, 65 to 75mm.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Close-Up (torso gone) or a Medium Shot (waist in). The tell is either a floating head or a belt buckle.

Fix: crop at the chest, keep a hand possible, keep a slice of room.

Questions

What is Medium Close-Up in film?

A medium close-up frames a person from the chest or shoulders up, at dialogue distance. You can still read shoulders and often a hand, while the face remains the primary information.

Medium Close-Up vs Medium Shot

A medium shot starts around the waist, so rest-position hands, a table, and a belt line are in. An MCU starts at the chest, so it is tighter talk coverage. If the belt is in, you have left MCU.

When should I use Medium Close-Up?

Use it when people talk and you still need body language without going waist-up. Do not use it for holster, gait, or a true facial fact that needs a close-up.

How do I prompt Medium Close-Up for AI image or video?

Write Medium close-up of [Subject] from chest up, dialogue distance, shoulders and hands still readable. Name 65 to 75mm if you want that working length. Keep the chest line in the shot.

entries.title: Medium Shot (MS)
entries.text:
Medium Shot (MS)

MSwaist shot

A medium shot frames a person from approximately the waist upward, so face and gesture share the rectangle. It is the workhorse size of coverage, sometimes called a waist shot.

Create this Medium Shot

Narrative function

Most scenes live in the medium shot because people talk with their hands. A glass, a phone, a cigarette, a slammed notebook all happen between waist and face.

Geography is still a little present (a booth, a window, a doorway) without becoming the subject. It is the wrong tool when the story is a walk, a costume from head to toe, or a face that must be the only landscape.

If you never leave this size, blocking becomes a radio play with heads and belts. Change size when the waist line no longer contains the fact.

How it works

Bottom frame at the waist or belt. Hands at rest should be in.

A 40mm to 50mm at conversational standing or sitting distance keeps perspective ordinary; the catalog 50mm is a default, not a law. Camera often at chest to eye height.

You should still read a bit of set, not a full room map. Prompt: Medium shot of [Subject] from the waist up, gesture and face in balance.

When to use it

Use it as workhorse coverage: overlapping dialogue, a booth conversation, someone waiting with a suitcase handle in frame. Do not use it when the information is a holster below the hip, the feet, or a micro-expression that needs a closer crop.

Compared with similar shots

A Medium Close-Up starts at the chest and throws the waist away. A Cowboy Shot drops the bottom frame to mid-thigh so hands at the holster line stay in.

Medium is the waist sentence, not MCU and not cowboy. A Close-Up is a different sentence entirely: the face outranks gesture.

Cowboy ShotShow hands, weapons, or stance without going full body.

Medium Close-UpTalk without losing body language.

Extreme Close-UpA detail is the scene: an eye, a mouth, a trigger.

In film

His Girl Friday runs talk and gesture in this band so overlapping dialogue still has cigarettes, phones, and desks. Lost in Translation uses waist-up hotel and bar distance where two people can exist without becoming portraits or wide maps.

Grammar: conversation with hands.

Prompt it

Say waist. Example: Medium shot of [Subject] from the waist up, conversational distance, 50mm, gesture and face in balance.

Do not write chest up, mid-thigh, or head and shoulders. For video, if the camera drifts down to the knees you have entered cowboy territory.

Use in Image Generator

Medium shot of [Subject] from the waist up, conversational distance, 50mm, gesture and face in balance.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Cowboy Shot (knees or mid-thigh in) or a Medium Close-Up (belt gone). The tell is either a gunbelt or a floating chest.

Fix: crop at the waist. Another tell is calling every talky frame a medium shot when it is an MCU.

Questions

What is Medium Shot in film?

A medium shot usually frames a person from the waist up so face and gesture share the frame. It is a size, sometimes called a waist shot, and it is the default band for a lot of scene coverage.

Medium Shot vs Cowboy Shot

A cowboy shot frames from mid-thigh or the knees up so hanging hands and a holster line remain. A medium shot cuts at the waist, so anything below the belt is out. If you can see thigh, you are not in a medium shot.

When should I use Medium Shot?

Use it when talk and hand business are the scene: tables, phones, glasses, notes. Do not use it when you need feet, a gunbelt, a full costume, or a face with no torso.

How do I prompt Medium Shot for AI image or video?

Write Medium shot of [Subject] from the waist up, conversational distance, 50mm. Keep hands in. Do not say cowboy, full body, or chest up.

entries.title: Cowboy Shot
entries.text:
Cowboy Shot

American shotknee shotmedium long shotthree-quarter shot

A cowboy shot frames a person from mid-thigh or the knees upward so the hands stay in at the holster line. It is also called an American shot or knee shot; it is not a waist shot and not a full figure.

Create this Cowboy Shot

Narrative function

The cowboy exists because hands are plot. A gun, a bottle, a fist, a coat hem at the thigh: the stance is the sentence.

You get face and threat or ease in one frame without spending the extra air that feet and floor demand. It is the wrong tool when gait, shoes, or the full costume silhouette is the information.

It is also the wrong tool for table talk: you will be cropping a booth at mid-thigh for no reason. Use it for standing confrontation, weapons, and posture, then go tighter for the eyes or wider for the walk.

How it works

Bottom frame through mid-thigh. Holster, hanging hands, and coat edge should read.

A 35mm to 50mm from a few steps back is common. Pairing with Hip Level puts the lens near the gunbelt; that height is a choice, not the size itself.

You can shoot a cowboy at eye height. Prompt: Cowboy shot of [Subject] framed mid-thigh up, hands visible at the holster line.

When to use it

Use it to show hands, weapons, or stance without going full body: a hand hovering at a belt, a bottle hanging, a ready posture. Do not use it if you need feet and walk, or if the beat is only a face.

Compared with similar shots

A Medium Shot cuts at the waist, so the holster and hanging hands are gone. A Full Body includes head to toe and a strip of floor.

Cowboy is the mid-thigh sentence: American shot, not MS, not full figure. Do not call it a medium long shot as if that erased the holster line.

Medium ShotWorkhorse coverage. Most scenes live here.

Full BodyCostume, blocking, and gait matter.

Extreme Close-UpA detail is the scene: an eye, a mouth, a trigger.

In film

The Good, the Bad and the Ugly uses this standing size so guns and faces share one frame before the eyes take over. Django Unchained keeps hands and weapons readable in the same band.

Grammar: stance plus face, not a landscape and not a waist-up talk shot.

Prompt it

Name mid-thigh and the hands. Example: Cowboy shot of [Subject] framed mid-thigh up, hands visible at the holster line, American shot.

Do not write waist up or head to toe. For video, if the feet enter you have left cowboy; if the belt is the bottom you have returned to medium.

Use in Image Generator

Cowboy shot of [Subject] framed mid-thigh up, hands visible at the holster line, American shot, casual authority.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Medium Shot (waist) or a Full Body (feet in). The tell is a belt-only crop, or shoes.

Fix: bottom frame through the thigh, hands in, feet out. Another tell is a sitting medium labeled cowboy because the genre is Western.

Questions

What is Cowboy Shot in film?

A cowboy shot frames a person from mid-thigh or knees up so the hands remain visible at the holster line. It is also called an American shot. It is a standing size for stance and weapons, not a synonym for medium or full body.

Cowboy Shot vs Full Body

Full body includes the feet and a little floor; the whole figure is complete. A cowboy stops at mid-thigh, so gait and shoes are out while hands stay in. If you can see boots on the ground, you have left cowboy.

When should I use Cowboy Shot?

Use it when hands, weapons, or stance matter and you do not need the walk. Do not use it for table dialogue or for costume-and-gait beats that require feet.

How do I prompt Cowboy Shot for AI image or video?

Write Cowboy shot of [Subject] framed mid-thigh up, hands visible at the holster line. Say American shot if that helps the model. Forbid feet and forbid a waist crop.

entries.title: Full Body (WS)
entries.text:
Full Body (WS)

long shotwide on personWSLS

A full body shot holds a person head to toe, with the figure complete and a readable strip of environment around the silhouette. The person is still the subject; the world is a border, not the owner of the frame.

Create this Full Body

Narrative function

Full body is for costume, blocking, and gait. You need the shoes, the hem, the way weight sits on a hip, the path to the door.

The figure occupies most of the frame height, so this is a portrait of a body in space, not a map of a valley. It is the wrong tool when land must dwarf the person, or when the beat is a face.

Calling every complete figure a long shot or a wide shot erases this size. If the human is still large in the rectangle and the feet are in, you are here.

If they have become a small mark in weather, you have gone longer.

How it works

Keep head and feet both in, with a little floor and a little air. The figure should own most of the vertical.

A 35mm to 50mm from enough distance avoids stretching the legs; a 24mm too close will cartoon the feet. Do not confuse this with a 24mm Wide room map.

Prompt: Full-body shot of [Subject], head to toe, figure complete in frame, environment readable around the silhouette.

When to use it

Use it when costume, blocking, and gait matter: a walk in a new coat, a stand in a doorway, a body that has to be seen whole. Do not use it when the land must win, or when you only needed mid-thigh for the hands.

Compared with similar shots

A Cowboy Shot stops at mid-thigh; feet are out. A Long Shot shows a full figure plus so much geography that the person is small in the world.

A Wide Shot lets place speak; bodies may be smaller still. Full body is the complete figure as subject, not cowboy, not long, not wide.

An Extreme Long Shot makes them a speck.

Cowboy ShotShow hands, weapons, or stance without going full body.

Extreme Long ShotScale is the emotion.

Extreme Close-UpA detail is the scene: an eye, a mouth, a trigger.

In film

The Searchers uses complete figures in doorways and desert edges so costume and stance read before the land fully claims them. Drive holds night walks head to toe so gait and scorpion jacket are the sentence.

Grammar: person complete, place as margin.

Prompt it

Say head to toe. Example: Full-body shot of [Subject], head to toe, figure complete in frame, environment readable around the silhouette.

Do not write long shot, wide, or mid-thigh. For video, if the figure shrinks into architecture you have drifted into a long shot.

Use in Image Generator

Full-body shot of [Subject], head to toe, figure complete in frame, environment readable around the silhouette.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Long Shot (person small in land) or a Cowboy Shot (no feet). The tell is a tiny figure in weather, or a crop at the knee.

Fix: feet in, head in, person still large in the frame. Do not label it WS or LS just because the body is complete.

Questions

What is Full Body in film?

A full body shot shows a person head to toe, with the figure complete and some environment around the silhouette. The human remains the subject. It is not the same as a long shot or a wide shot, even if those names get used loosely.

Full Body vs Long Shot

In a full body shot the person fills most of the height; place is a readable border. In a long shot the full figure sits in substantial geography and could be ignored by the world. If the human is small in the rectangle, you have left full body.

When should I use Full Body?

Use it for costume, blocking, and gait. Do not use it when scale or landscape should dominate, and do not use it when hands-at-holster would have been enough.

How do I prompt Full Body for AI image or video?

Write Full-body shot of [Subject], head to toe, figure complete in frame, environment readable around the silhouette. Forbid a speck-in-landscape result. Keep feet visible.

entries.title: Long Shot (WS)
entries.text:
Long Shot (WS)

wide shotWSLS

A long shot in cinematography shows the full subject plus a substantial portion of the environment, so a person sits small in geography. The figure is still locatable as a human; the world is large enough to ignore them.

Create this Long Shot

Narrative function

A long shot places a human in a world that could continue without them. You still recognize a body, a walk, a horse, but land, street, or weather takes most of the rectangle.

The sentence is person-in-world, not person-as-portrait. It is the wrong tool when you need the face, the holster, or a complete figure that still owns the height of the frame.

It is also the wrong tool when the person has become an unreadable speck: that is farther still. Use it to locate a body in a place, then go closer for the decision.

How it works

Keep a full figure readable, then add enough architecture or terrain that the person does not fill the height. Working from farther back with a 24mm to 35mm, or from a ridge with a longer lens, both can get you here; the crop is the size.

Deep enough focus that the place reads. Prompt: Long shot of [Subject] small in a large environment, full figure plus geography.

When to use it

Use it to place a human in a world that could ignore them: a rider on a ridge, a coat on a platform, a body in a square. Do not use it to read an eyelid, and do not use it when you only needed head-to-toe as a portrait.

Compared with similar shots

A Full Body keeps the person large, head to toe, with place as a border. A Wide Shot is environment-forward coverage: place still speaks, often as the map of a scene.

An Extreme Long Shot turns the figure into a speck and gives the land the subject. Long shot is full figure plus geography, not those three.

An Establishing Shot is a job (where and when), which may use this size.

Extreme Long ShotScale is the emotion.

Establishing ShotOpen a scene. Tell us where and when.

Extreme Close-UpA detail is the scene: an eye, a mouth, a trigger.

In film

Lawrence of Arabia sets riders in desert so the person is still a figure and the land is already huge. Seven Samurai plants bodies in village dirt and fields the same way.

Grammar: locatable human, large world, not a postage-stamp speck and not a costume portrait.

Prompt it

Say full figure plus geography. Example: Long shot of [Subject] small in a large environment, full figure plus geography.

Do not write head to toe as a hero portrait, and do not write speck against vast terrain. For video, keep the body identifiable; if they vanish into texture, you have gone to extreme long shot.

Use in Image Generator

Long shot of [Subject] small in a large environment, full figure plus geography, mythic placement of a person in land.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Full Body (person fills the height) or an Extreme Long Shot (speck). The tell is either a fashion lookbook figure or a landscape with no readable human.

Fix: full figure visible, world dominant, person still a person.

Questions

What is Long Shot in film?

A long shot shows a full subject and a substantial portion of the environment, so a person is small in a large place but still readable as a figure. It is a size, not automatically an establishing shot.

Long Shot vs Wide Shot

A long shot is the person-in-world size: full figure plus geography. A wide shot is environment-forward coverage whose job is to let place speak and not isolate yet. They overlap in the wild, but wide is a coverage attitude; long is the figure-plus-land sentence.

When should I use Long Shot?

Use it to locate a human in a place large enough to ignore them. Do not use it for faces, and do not use it when you wanted a full-body portrait or a speck-scale landscape.

How do I prompt Long Shot for AI image or video?

Write Long shot of [Subject] small in a large environment, full figure plus geography. Keep the body identifiable. Do not say head-to-toe hero and do not say speck.

entries.title: Extreme Long Shot (ELS)
entries.text:
Extreme Long Shot (ELS)

ELSextreme wideEWSExtreme-wide scale contrast

An extreme long shot makes environment, scale, geography, or isolation dominant over individual detail. A person, if present, is a speck: a scale mark, not a portrait.

Create this Extreme Long Shot

Narrative function

An ELS turns size into the emotion: awe, insignificance, loneliness, ambition. The small anchor lets the audience measure a space that would otherwise be abstract.

The land, the station, the spillway, or the void is the subject. It is the wrong tool when you still need a face, a costume, or even a clearly posed full figure.

It is also the wrong tool without a readable reference: huge architecture with no human, vehicle, or known object can look like a miniature. Use it when scale is the point, then come in when a person must act.

How it works

Keep the scale reference detectable through contrast, motion, or placement. Deep focus so terrain layers read; without depth cues the space flattens into a model.

An Aerial Pullback can arrive here by moving; the size itself can be a lock-off from a ridge or a high vantage. Prompt: Extreme long shot of [Subject] as a speck against vast terrain, landscape as the true subject.

When to use it

Use it when scale is the emotion: a yellow coat at the base of a spillway, a rider swallowed by desert, a craft against a planet. Do not omit a readable reference object, and do not use it to cover dialogue.

Compared with similar shots

A Long Shot still presents a locatable full figure in large geography. A Wide Shot lets place speak inside coverage; bodies are small but not necessarily specks.

An Establishing Shot is a function that often uses this size but can also be a sign or a building. ELS is speck-scale.

Aerial Pullback is a move that can end on this size.

Aerial PullbackClose a chapter. Geography wins.

Establishing ShotOpen a scene. Tell us where and when.

Extreme Close-UpA detail is the scene: an eye, a mouth, a trigger.

In film

Lawrence of Arabia lets figures and riders occupy vast desert until they are marks in sand. 2001: A Space Odyssey sets small human or spacecraft elements against immense environments.

Nomadland uses wide country the same way: the van and the body as scale, the land as subject. Grammar: measure the world, do not portrait the person.

Lawrence of Arabia 1962Figures and riders occupy vast expanses of desert.

2001: A Space Odyssey 1968Small human or spacecraft elements are set against immense environments.

Prompt it

Say speck and name the terrain. Example: Extreme long shot of [Subject] as a speck against vast terrain, infinite depth of field, landscape as the true subject.

Demand a detectable human-scale reference. For video, a tiny walk or a dust veil helps the figure read; a locked empty canyon with no marker will look like a maquette.

Use in Video Generator

Extreme-wide static shot of a lone surveyor in a yellow coat at the base of an enormous concrete spillway. The figure is tiny but unmistakable; immense walls recede naturally. Slow drifting mist, no camera move, no giant-person scale errors.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Long Shot (person still a clear figure) or an Establishing Shot that is really a building postcard with no scale. The tell is a readable full-body pose, or a vast space that looks like a tabletop.

Fix: shrink the human to a mark, keep them findable, add depth cues.

Questions

What is Extreme Long Shot in film?

An extreme long shot makes environment and scale the subject, with any person reduced to a small reference in a much larger landscape or structure. Individual facial detail is gone on purpose.

Extreme Long Shot vs Long Shot

A long shot still shows a full, locatable figure in large geography. An extreme long shot makes that figure a speck and hands the frame to terrain, architecture, or sky. If you can costume-read the person, you are probably still in long shot.

When should I use Extreme Long Shot?

Use it when scale is the emotion and you have a readable human or object as a measuring stick. Do not use it for talk, and do not shoot empty vastness with no reference.

How do I prompt Extreme Long Shot for AI image or video?

Write Extreme long shot of [Subject] as a speck against vast terrain, landscape as the true subject. Keep the scale reference detectable. Ask for deep focus and environmental depth cues so it does not look like a miniature.

entries.title: Establishing Shot
entries.text:
Establishing Shot

opening establishing shotre-establishing shotaerial establishing shotTransitional still lifeUnpeopled interval

An establishing shot introduces or re-establishes location, geography, time of day, or social context. It is a job in the sequence, not a synonym for wide or extreme long shot.

Volume

Create this Establishing Shot

Narrative function

Before coverage begins, or when a scene has drifted, the audience needs to know where and when. An establishing shot declares the building, the street, the hour, the weather, sometimes the class of the place.

A later re-establishing shot can remind us of the same geography after the scene has moved. It is the wrong tool when you actually needed the skeleton of the action: that is a master.

It is also the wrong tool as empty postcard filler. Not every empty room is a pillow shot; placement and duration create the function.

A clock, a sign, or a doorway can establish. A huge landscape that never connects to the next cut does not.

How it works

Choose a vantage that names spatial relations: who can reach which door, which way is the city, what the light is doing. Often a Wide Shot or Extreme Long Shot, sometimes a facade, an aerial, or an unpeopled interval.

Hold long enough to read time of day. Preserve ambient sound in editorial thinking even if you are prompting a still.

Prompt: Wide establishing shot of [Subject] and the location at once, time of day and spatial relations declared before coverage begins.

When to use it

Use it to open a scene or to tell us where and when: a hotel at blue hour, a jury building in morning smog, a re-establish after a time jump. Do not fire one on every recut if geography has not changed, and do not confuse it with a master that must play the scene.

Compared with similar shots

A Master Shot covers the dramatic action and blocking of this scene. An establishing shot names the place and time; it does not have to contain the argument.

An Extreme Long Shot is a size that often does this job. A Wide Shot is environment-forward coverage inside a scene, not automatically an establish.

A Long Shot places a person in land; that may or may not be the first image of the location.

Extreme Long ShotScale is the emotion.

Master ShotProtect the scene. You can always go tighter.

Extreme Close-UpA detail is the scene: an eye, a mouth, a trigger.

In film

Blade Runner opens on a city that is already a time and a social order. The Shining uses the Overlook approach as geography before the interiors take over.

Tokyo Story and Late Spring let empty rooms and streets punctuate, which is related grammar: the world persisting between people. Peking Opera Blues reestablishes a party in broader views.

Use those as where-and-when grammar, not as frames to copy.

Tokyo Story 1953Empty rooms, streets and industrial views punctuate the family narrative.

Late Spring 1949Still-life and room imagery interrupts or outlasts the human exchange.

Peking Opera Blues 1986The opening party is introduced and later reestablished in broader views.

12 Angry Men 1957Wider room views clarify the changing jury arrangement.

Black Narcissus 1947The Himalayan convent and vertiginous cliff environments.

Star Wars 1977Large hangar and space-station environments extend beyond the built sets.

Prompt it

Declare place and time. Example: Wide establishing shot of [Subject] and the location at once, time of day and spatial relations declared before coverage begins.

Name the hour, the weather, and what building or street this is. For video, a small environmental motion (traffic, steam, a flag) is enough; do not tour if the job is only to plant geography.

Use in Video Generator

After a daughter leaves the house, hold a static shot of the empty entryway: her shoes are gone, afternoon light remains on the floor and distant street noise continues. No person enters, no camera move, no sentimental insert music. Cut to the next scene only after the room has registered as its own space.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Master Shot (action skeleton) or a pretty Extreme Long Shot with no relation to the next cut. The tell is a landscape postcard, or a wide that already plays the whole scene and gets labeled establish.

Fix: the shot should answer where and when, then coverage can begin.

Questions

What is Establishing Shot in film?

An establishing shot introduces or re-establishes location, geography, time, or social context. It is a function in the edit. It is often wide, but a sign, a clock, or a building can do the same job.

Establishing Shot vs Master Shot

A master covers the complete dramatic action and spatial blocking so you could play the scene in that one setup. An establishing shot tells you where and when, and does not have to contain the argument. You can cut from an establish into a master, or skip one if geography is already known.

When should I use Establishing Shot?

Use it to open a scene or to re-establish after a jump in time or place. Do not insert one as decoration on every reverse, and do not use it when you actually needed the scene's action covered in a master.

How do I prompt Establishing Shot for AI image or video?

Write Wide establishing shot of [Subject] and the location at once, and name time of day and spatial relations. Put the place in the sentence, not only the person. Keep the next coverage in mind so the geography matches.

entries.title: Master Shot
entries.text:
Master Shot

wide mastermoving mastermaster scene

A master shot covers the complete dramatic action and the spatial geography of a scene in one setup. It is the skeleton you can play in full, then cut into.

Create this Master Shot

Narrative function

A master protects the scene. If every close-up dies, you still have who sat where, who could reach the door, and how the argument moved through the room.

It is usually wide enough for blocking, not so wide that faces and props stop meaning anything. It is the wrong tool when you only needed to name the building from outside: that is an establish.

It is also the wrong tool as a lifeless wide you never intend to use, parked for safety while all the acting happens in mismatched singles. A moving master can carry the whole beat if blocking and camera path are designed together.

How it works

Set a camera that sees all essential blocking: seats, door, table, the path out. Size is often a Wide Shot or a loose Two-Shot, but the job is coverage of the action, not a particular crop.

Keep faces and key props readable enough to cut. Mark the 180.

You can later cut in or go to singles. Prompt: Wide master of [Subject] with all blocking visible, the skeleton of the scene in one continuous frame, coverage can cut in later.

When to use it

Use it to protect the scene: a jury room argument that could play in one take, a party whose crossings you must understand. Do not skip it and hope singles will invent geography, and do not treat an exterior postcard as a master.

Compared with similar shots

An Establishing Shot says where and when; a master says what happens in this space. A Wide Shot is a size.

A Two-Shot may be the master if two people and their blocking are the whole scene. A Group Shot shows an ensemble as a unit; it is a master only if the complete action plays inside it.

You can always go tighter. You cannot always invent a door that was never in the skeleton.

Establishing ShotOpen a scene. Tell us where and when.

Two-ShotThe relationship is the shot.

Extreme Close-UpA detail is the scene: an eye, a mouth, a trigger.

In film

12 Angry Men keeps returning to roomy views that clarify the changing jury arrangement so singles have a map. Nashville builds scenes whose wider coverage holds crossings and music as one geography.

Grammar: the scene could play here.

Prompt it

Demand all blocking. Example: Wide master of [Subject] with all blocking visible, the skeleton of the scene in one continuous frame.

Name the door, the table, and who stands where. For video, let the action play; do not punch in.

Coverage can be generated as later sizes from the same geography.

Use in Image Generator

Wide master of [Subject] with all blocking visible, the skeleton of the scene in one continuous frame, coverage can cut in later.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is an Establishing Shot (place, no action) or a Wide Shot that crops out the door you will need. The tell is a pretty exterior, or a wide so empty that the scene cannot play.

Fix: every important path and body must be in, and the take must be able to run the beat.

Questions

What is Master Shot in film?

A master shot is a setup that covers the complete dramatic action and spatial geography of a scene. It is the skeleton of the scene, often wide, and you can cut in tighter coverage later.

Master Shot vs Establishing Shot

An establishing shot introduces location and time. A master covers the action inside the scene: who moves where, who can reach whom. A skyline cannot be your master if the argument happens in a kitchen.

When should I use Master Shot?

Use it to protect the scene so geography and blocking remain true. Do not confuse it with an exterior establish, and do not shoot a lifeless wide you never intended to play.

How do I prompt Master Shot for AI image or video?

Write Wide master of [Subject] with all blocking visible, the skeleton of the scene in one continuous frame. Name furniture, doors, and positions. For video, play the whole beat in that frame.

entries.title: Two-Shot
entries.text:
Two-Shot

profile two-shotwalking two-shotlayered two-shotShared frame instead of isolated faces

A two-shot, or two shot, frames two principal subjects together so their distance and posture can be compared in one composition. The space between them is part of the sentence.

Volume

Create this Two-Shot

Narrative function

When the relationship is the shot, cutting to singles too soon steals the audience's ability to watch both people at once. A two-shot lets the viewer choose which face to read, and it makes a lean, a flinch, or a widening gap visible without an edit.

It is the wrong tool when one person must own the frame, or when a third body is politically in the scene. It is also the wrong tool as a timid wide that hides both performances.

Keep head sizes readable. Profile, 50-50, walking, or layered (one nearer) are variants of the same job: two people, one picture.

How it works

Balance or deliberately unbalance head sizes. Set a readable axis.

40mm to 50mm at table or walking distance is common. Decide whether one face is privileged by focus or light.

Small changes in distance are the acting. Prompt: Two-shot of [Subject] with a second figure, the space between them doing narrative work, 50mm, shared frame as relationship.

When to use it

Use it when the relationship is the shot: two people at a diner table, a walk, a shared silence. Do not hide both faces in an unnecessarily empty wide, and do not use a two-shot if the scene has become a trio.

Compared with similar shots

Over-the-shoulder coverage puts one face in focus and the partner as a foreground shoulder; it is not a shared two-person portrait. A Single removes the partner.

A Three-Shot adds a third principal and a new politics. Two-shot means both people author the frame.

Shot/reverse is an editing pattern, not this size.

Three-ShotA trio has politics.

Extreme Close-UpA detail is the scene: an eye, a mouth, a trigger.

Choker ShotEmotion with nowhere to hide.

In film

Heat plants two opponents across one diner table before and between singles, so the gap is visible. Persona juxtaposes faces inside severe shared compositions.

Before Sunrise and The Apartment keep pairs in one frame so walking and apartment air are the relation. Grammar: two bodies, one sentence.

Persona 1966Faces are juxtaposed and related within severe shared compositions.

Heat 1995The diner encounter establishes two opponents across one table before and between singles.

Prompt it

Demand two people and the gap. Example: Two-shot of [Subject] with a second figure, the space between them doing narrative work, 50mm.

Specify profile, facing, or layered. Keep both faces readable unless you are hiding one on purpose.

For video, let distance change; do not cut to singles inside the prompt if you want the shared frame to hold.

Use in Video Generator

Hold a medium profile two-shot of two former business partners seated across a narrow café table. Both faces remain readable at once. One leans forward while the other slowly leans back. No cutting to singles, no focus change, tension expressed through changing distance.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Over-the-Shoulder Coverage (one face plus a shoulder) or two singles cut together. The tell is one sharp face and a blur of coat, or both people so small the relation dies.

Fix: two principals, comparable scale, the gap visible.

Questions

What is Two-Shot in film?

A two-shot frames two principal subjects together so their relationship, distance, and posture are visible in one composition. The space between them is part of the shot, not only the faces.

Two-Shot vs Over-the-Shoulder Coverage

A two-shot gives both people authorship of the frame. Over-the-shoulder coverage uses a near shoulder as a foreground fragment while the far face is the subject. If you only see one face clearly, you are in OTS, not a two-shot.

When should I use Two-Shot?

Use it when the relationship is the event and the audience should watch both people at once. Do not use it as a timid wide that hides acting, and do not use it for a three-person politics problem.

How do I prompt Two-Shot for AI image or video?

Write Two-shot of [Subject] with a second figure, the space between them doing narrative work. Name whether they are in profile, facing, or layered. Keep both faces readable.

entries.title: Three-Shot
entries.text:
Three-Shot

A three-shot, or three shot, frames three principal subjects together, usually so alliances and the odd one out are readable in the blocking. It is a group sentence of three, not three singles cut together.

Create this Three-Shot

Narrative function

A trio has politics. Two against one, a hinge person in the middle, a late arrival who splits a pair: the triangle is the story.

If you only cover this as ping-pong singles, the audience never sees who is left out in real space. It is the wrong tool when there are four or more as a unit, or when the scene has collapsed to a pair.

It is also the wrong tool if you line three heads up with equal light and equal height and call that drama. Someone should own a peak of the triangle, or stand in the cold of it.

How it works

Arrange three bodies as a triangle in depth or across the frame, not a flat police lineup unless the story is a firing squad. Triangular Composition helps, but blocking comes first: seats, levels, who faces whom.

Keep all three faces or postures readable enough to compare. Prompt: Three-shot of [Subject] in a triangular group, alliances and the odd one out readable in blocking.

When to use it

Use it when a trio has politics: three gunmen, three people at a verdict, a couple plus the person who should not be there. Do not flatten them into equal portraits, and do not use a three-shot for a crowd.

Compared with similar shots

A Two-Shot is a pair; adding a third changes the grammar. A Group Shot holds a small ensemble larger than three as a relational unit.

A Master Shot may be a three-shot if the whole action is those three bodies. Do not treat three-shot as a synonym for any wide with extra extras.

Two-ShotThe relationship is the shot.

Group ShotA family, a crew, a jury.

Extreme Close-UpA detail is the scene: an eye, a mouth, a trigger.

In film

The Good, the Bad and the Ugly is the textbook trio: three men, three distances, one cemetery geometry. The standoff only works because all three remain comparable in shared frames before the eyes take over.

Grammar: three principals, readable alliance.

Prompt it

Name three and the triangle. Example: Three-shot of [Subject] in a triangular group, alliances and the odd one out readable in blocking.

Specify who is isolated by height, light, or gap. For video, a small blocking shift (one step back) should change the politics without a cut.

Use in Image Generator

Three-shot of [Subject] in a triangular group, alliances and the odd one out readable in blocking.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Two-Shot that crops the third, or a Group Shot with extras filling the sides. The tell is two faces and a shoulder, or a crowd.

Fix: three principals, triangular blocking, one of them slightly out.

Questions

What is Three-Shot in film?

A three-shot frames three principal people in one composition so their alliances, blocking, and who is left out are readable. It is not three close-ups in a row.

Three-Shot vs Two-Shot

A two-shot is a pair and the space between them. A three-shot adds a third principal and a triangle of politics. If the third person is only an out-of-focus extra, you still have a two-shot.

When should I use Three-Shot?

Use it when the scene's power is three-way: alliances, a hinge, an odd one out. Do not use it for a pair, and do not use it as a stand-in for a larger ensemble.

How do I prompt Three-Shot for AI image or video?

Write Three-shot of [Subject] in a triangular group, alliances and the odd one out readable in blocking. Name who is isolated. Keep all three readable.

entries.title: Group Shot
entries.text:
Group Shot

A group shot frames a small ensemble as a relational unit, such as a family, a crew, or a jury. Position, height, and light say who belongs and who dominates.

Create this Group Shot

Narrative function

A group shot is not a crowd still. It is a unit: people who share a table, a job, a crime, a bloodline.

The audience should be able to rank them at a glance: who sits, who stands, who is brightest, who is at the edge. It is the wrong tool when the politics are only two or three principals, or when you needed a master of action rather than a portrait of the unit.

Lighting everyone the same makes a yearbook. Let one face own the key, or let depth split generations.

How it works

Stage in layers: seated foreground, standing mid, a doorway back. Who is highest, central, nearest, brightest.

A slightly wider lens (35mm to 50mm) holds the unit without turning them into ants; go longer if you want compression to stack them. Prompt: Group shot containing [Subject] among several figures, ensemble blocking, who owns the frame by position and light.

When to use it

Use it for a family, a crew, a jury: the unit as the subject. Do not light every face equally if someone owns the room, and do not use a group shot when the beat has become a two-person fight.

Compared with similar shots

A Three-Shot is specifically three principals. A Master Shot covers the complete action; a group shot may be that master, or it may be a posed unit inside a larger scene.

A Two-Shot is a pair. Group means the ensemble is the relation, usually more than three, still small enough to read as people rather than a mob.

Three-ShotA trio has politics.

Master ShotProtect the scene. You can always go tighter.

Extreme Close-UpA detail is the scene: an eye, a mouth, a trigger.

In film

The Godfather stages families and crews so rank is seating, light, and who gets the center. Parasite uses household groupings the same way: who serves, who sits, who stands in a doorway.

Grammar: the unit, ranked.

Prompt it

Name the unit and the owner. Example: Group shot containing [Subject] among several figures, ensemble blocking, who owns the frame by position and light.

Specify count (five at a table, a crew of six) and who is brightest or highest. For video, a small shift in who stands can re-rank the group without a cut.

Use in Image Generator

Group shot containing [Subject] among several figures, ensemble blocking, who owns the frame by position and light.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Three-Shot labeled group, or a Master Shot so wide the faces die. The tell is three people, or a mob with no rank.

Fix: a small ensemble, readable faces, one person owning position or key.

Questions

What is Group Shot in film?

A group shot frames a small ensemble as one relational unit so belonging and dominance read through blocking and light. It is more than a trio, still small enough that people remain individuals.

Group Shot vs Three-Shot

A three-shot is three principals and their triangle. A group shot is a larger unit: family, crew, jury. If you only have three named people, write three-shot. If the unit is the household or the crew, write group.

When should I use Group Shot?

Use it when the ensemble is the subject and rank should be visible. Do not use it for a pair or a trio, and do not flatten everyone with equal light.

How do I prompt Group Shot for AI image or video?

Write Group shot containing [Subject] among several figures, ensemble blocking, who owns the frame by position and light. Give a head count and name the dominant body.

entries.title: Insert Shot
entries.text:
Insert Shot

Pursued objectPlot-driving objective

An insert shot is a close view of a story-relevant detail: an object, a hand action, a screen, or text. It points at the thing that will matter, at real scale.

Volume

Create this Insert Shot

Narrative function

An insert is not a pretty prop break. It is a fact the wider coverage cannot prove: the handwriting, the latch, the cup of water beginning to tremble, the key in a palm.

Hands should be human-sized. The object should cut with the same key as the scene.

It is the wrong tool when you are leaving the action for a clock on the wall or a listener in another room: that is a cutaway. It is also the wrong tool as a glowing product hero.

If the object's specific mechanism never pays off, you may only have a MacGuffin in the plot, but the insert still has to be a readable picture of a thing.

How it works

Size to the object. Match the scene's key side and color so the cut belongs.

Macro only if the detail is small; a letter can be a close crop on a 50mm. Keep hands at real scale, no giant fingers.

Prompt: Tight close-up of an object that carries the plot near [Subject]: a glass, a letter, a latch. Hands at real scale.

No glowing skin.

When to use it

Use it to point at the thing that will matter later: a key, a letter, a latch, a trembling glass. Do not insert a decorative object that never returns, and do not light it like a catalog hero if it lives in a messy room.

Compared with similar shots

A Cutaway leaves the primary action for context, a clock, or an observer. An Extreme Close-Up is a size; an insert is a job and may be that tight.

A cut-in tightens on something already proven in the wider shot, often on the same axis. A Gesture covers a body movement rather than an object.

Product lighting treats the object as a commercial portrait, which is a different job.

CutawayHide a cut, show a clock, or let the room comment.

Extreme Close-UpA detail is the scene: an eye, a mouth, a trigger.

Choker ShotEmotion with nowhere to hide.

In film

Rear Window uses optical details as plot facts. Zodiac lives in handwriting and paper.

Notorious makes a concealed key a crucial object. Jurassic Park lets water in a cup reveal an approaching vibration.

The Maltese Falcon and North by Northwest organize pursuit around objects; those are story engines, while the insert is the picture of the thing. Grammar: show the fact.

The Maltese Falcon 1941The sought-after statuette organizes competing loyalties.

North by Northwest 1959The espionage material matters chiefly through the pursuit surrounding it.

Notorious 1946The concealed key becomes a crucial object.

Citizen Kane 1941The sled and its inscription matter at the ending.

Jurassic Park 1993Water in the cup reveals an approaching vibration.

Prompt it

Name the object and the scale. Example: Tight close-up of an object that carries the plot near [Subject]: a glass, a letter, a latch.

Hands at real scale. No glowing skin.

Match the room's key. For video, a small physical change (a tremor, a thumb on a latch) is the motion; do not orbit the prop.

Use in Video Generator

Outline a short caper around an unopened blue envelope sought by three strangers. Never reveal its contents. Build the scenes around shifting trust, mistaken possession and one character choosing a friend over the envelope. Generate a consistent, easily trackable prop for every shot.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Cutaway (leaving the action) or a Product hero (catalog glamour). The tell is a clock in another room, or black-sweep reflections on a plot letter.

Fix: same scene, same light, object at real scale, story reason to look.

Questions

What is Insert Shot in film?

An insert shot is a close view of a story-relevant detail, object, hand action, screen, or text. It is coverage of a plot fact, usually cut into a wider scene, with hands and objects at real scale.

Insert Shot vs Cutaway

An insert stays on a detail that belongs to the primary action: the letter in the hands, the latch, the glass. A cutaway leaves that action for a related piece of the world, such as a clock, a street, or a listener. If you have left the actor's beat, you are probably in a cutaway.

When should I use Insert Shot?

Use it when a detail will matter and the wide cannot prove it. Do not use it as decoration, and do not use it when you meant to leave the scene for context.

How do I prompt Insert Shot for AI image or video?

Write Tight close-up of an object that carries the plot near [Subject], name the object, and specify hands at real scale. Match the scene light. No catalog glow.

entries.title: Cutaway
entries.text:
Cutaway

Plan de coupe

A cutaway shot leaves the primary action for a related detail, observer, or part of the same world. It is used for context, reaction, compression, or continuity repair.

Volume

Create this Cutaway

Narrative function

A cutaway is a brief exit: a clock, a kettle, a street, a person listening in a doorway. Its value is the relation it adds, not merely that it hides a bad join.

It can build anticipation, let the room comment, or imply that time has passed. It is the wrong tool when the object is the plot in the actor's hands: that is an insert.

It is also the wrong tool if the return to the main action restarts a gesture that should have continued. Check temporal logic.

A cutaway can be a pressure release; it can also cheat geography if the new view could not exist at that moment.

How it works

Choose a detail that can plausibly be present now. Match ambient light and, in editorial thinking, room sound.

Return to the main action at a later phase of the motion, not at the same frame of a handshake. Prompt: Cutaway from [Subject] to a related detail in the same world, a pressure-release or information beat that is not an insert on the actor.

When to use it

Use it to hide a cut, show a clock, or let the room comment: a kettle trembling during an argument, a courtyard while someone looks. Do not cut away to a new geography that implies false time, and do not call an object-in-hand a cutaway.

Compared with similar shots

An Insert Shot stays on a plot object inside the action. A Reaction Shot is a person's response, often a face; a cutaway might be that listener, or it might be a non-human detail.

A cut-in goes tighter on something already in the master, same space and often same axis, without leaving the beat. Cutaway means you left.

Insert ShotPoint at the thing that will matter later.

Reaction ShotThe important action is watching.

Extreme Close-UpA detail is the scene: an eye, a mouth, a trigger.

In film

Hot Fuzz uses cutaways as both joke and glue. The Conversation lets the world around a listener comment.

Dancer in the Dark brackets a car conversation with wider and closer views. Jurassic Park punctuates approaching threat with environmental details and observers.

Grammar: leave, add a relation, return honestly.

Dancer in the Dark 2000Wider and closer views bracket the conversation in Bill’s car.

Jurassic Park 1993Environmental details and observers punctuate the approaching threat.

Prompt it

Name the exit. Example: Cutaway from [Subject] to a related detail in the same world (a clock, a kettle, a street, a listener), not an insert on the actor.

Match the key. For video, hold the detail, then imply a return; do not keep the original action in frame if you meant to leave it.

Use in Video Generator

A couple argues quietly in a kitchen. Cut away to a kettle beginning to tremble on the stove while their voices continue, then return to the couple after a tense pause. Generate the insert separately with matching light and room sound. No literal symbolism captions.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is an Insert Shot (object in the action) or a random pretty detail. The tell is a letter in the hero's hands labeled cutaway, or a return that rewinds the action.

Fix: leave the primary beat, pick a plausible now, watch time on the way back.

Questions

What is Cutaway in film?

A cutaway is a shot away from the primary action, used for context, reaction, compression, or continuity repair. It might be a clock, a street, an observer, or a piece of the room.

Cutaway vs Insert Shot

An insert is a close view of a story object or hand fact inside the action. A cutaway leaves that action for a related view. Hands on the plot letter are an insert; the kettle on the stove during the fight is a cutaway.

When should I use Cutaway?

Use it to add a relation, hide a join, compress time, or let the world comment. Do not use it to show the object in the actor's hands, and do not return in a way that rewinds the action.

How do I prompt Cutaway for AI image or video?

Write Cutaway from [Subject] to a related detail in the same world, and name that detail. Say it is not an insert on the actor. Match light to the main scene.

entries.title: Reaction Shot
entries.text:
Reaction Shot

Kuleshov effectAssociative reaction construction

A reaction shot shows a character's response to an event, a line, or an unseen stimulus. The important action is watching; the face (or body) is the cut.

Volume

Create this Reaction Shot

Narrative function

A reaction shot is coverage of receiving. The gunshot, the insult, the courtyard window: we often learn what it meant by looking at the person who saw it.

Meaning can be constructed between shots. A relatively still face reads differently depending on what came before, which is the Kuleshov lesson, not a demand that you fake a historical clip.

It is the wrong tool when the speaker's line still needs to be seen, or when you over-act the response so the audience is told the emotion. It is a function, not a size: often a close-up, sometimes an MCU, occasionally a full-body flinch.

How it works

Point the eyeline at the stimulus, even if that stimulus is offscreen. Hold.

Minimize explanatory mugging if you want the cut to do the work. Match Look Space and eyeline to the previous shot.

Size is usually Close-Up or Medium Close-Up. Prompt: Reaction close-up of [Subject] receiving news they cannot speak yet, the face as the cut.

When to use it

Use it when the important action is watching: the face after an offscreen shot, the listener who cannot speak yet. Do not use it as a blink after every clause, and do not perform the entire emotion so the juxtaposition has nothing to do.

Compared with similar shots

A Close-Up is a size; a reaction is why that size is here. Over-the-shoulder coverage still includes the partner as a shoulder; a reaction single can drop them.

A Cutaway may be a non-human comment; a reaction is a person's response. Keep the face fixed if you want to test Kuleshov; changing the expression changes the experiment.

Close-UpRead micro-expression. Default for important dialogue.

Extreme Close-UpA detail is the scene: an eye, a mouth, a trigger.

Choker ShotEmotion with nowhere to hide.

In film

The Godfather often lets receiving carry the beat. Whiplash cuts to the face that has to survive the next bar.

Rear Window builds Jeff's looks so courtyard views change what the same face means. Grammar: watch the watcher.

Rear Window 1954Jeff’s looks acquire different meanings through the courtyard views placed beside them.

Prompt it

Name receiving. Example: Reaction close-up of [Subject] receiving news they cannot speak yet, the face as the cut.

Specify eyeline offscreen or toward a known object. For video, hold a small physical change (a swallow, a blink) rather than a tour of expressions.

Use in Video Generator

Generate one neutral close-up of a woman looking slightly down and right. Reuse the identical clip in three short edits: after a broken heirloom, after a sleeping puppy and after an unsigned contract. Generate the inserts separately and keep the reaction genuinely unchanged. Compare the meanings created by the juxtaposition.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a generic Close-Up of the speaker, or an overplayed grimace. The tell is mouth moving through the line, or eyebrows explaining the plot.

Fix: this person is receiving, not delivering. Point the eyes; hold.

Questions

What is Reaction Shot in film?

A reaction shot shows a character's response to an event, a line, or an unseen stimulus. It is a coverage function: the important action is watching, and the face or body is what the cut is about.

Reaction Shot vs Close-Up

A close-up is a crop: head and upper shoulders. A reaction shot is a job: this image exists because of what was just seen or heard. Reactions are often close-ups, but a close-up of someone speaking is not a reaction.

When should I use Reaction Shot?

Use it when watching is the event and the audience should read the receiver. Do not stack one after every sentence, and do not over-act the face if the cut is supposed to supply meaning.

How do I prompt Reaction Shot for AI image or video?

Write Reaction close-up of [Subject] receiving news they cannot speak yet, the face as the cut. Put the eyeline in the prompt. Keep the expression restrained unless the scene needs a big flinch.

entries.title: Over-the-Shoulder Coverage (OTS)
entries.text:
Over-the-Shoulder Coverage (OTS)

OTSAmorce épaule

Over-the-shoulder coverage, or an over the shoulder shot, puts a near shoulder or head in the foreground while the far face stays sharp. Paired reverses preserve relational space.

Volume

Create this Over-the-Shoulder Coverage

Narrative function

OTS is default dialogue coverage with spatial glue. The partner remains physically present even in a close view.

Shoulder size and how much it obstructs can make the observer feel dominant, intimate, or trapped. It is the wrong tool when you need to isolate someone as if the other person had left the room: that is a clean single.

It is also the wrong tool if both faces are equally sharp and complete: that is a two-shot. An over-the-shoulder shot is a framing choice.

Shot/reverse shot is an editing pattern. They are not synonyms.

How it works

Place the camera beside one body, looking past a soft near shoulder at the far face. The far person looks at the near person, toward that shoulder, never into the lens.

Match foreground body position, head size, and eyeline on the reverse. The 180-degree line is the axis between the two bodies.

OTS coverage lives on one side of that line. If the near shoulder sits camera-right, the far face looks camera-right.

The reverse OTS swaps who is near, but it stays on the same side of the axis so screen direction does not flip. Crossing the line is not a style choice in this coverage: it makes two people look like they share a bench instead of a conversation.

Use focus and lighting to keep the speaking face sharp and the near cloth soft. Prompt: Over-the-shoulder framing of [Subject], near shoulder soft in foreground, the far face sharp, looking toward the near shoulder, 180-line held.

Never cross the 180-degree line. Draw the axis between the two people and keep the camera on one side of it. Far face looks at the near shoulder. The reverse stays on the same side of the axis. If they look into the lens or away from each other, it is no longer OTS coverage.

When to use it

Use it as default dialogue coverage when you want the relationship to stay in the picture: a diner, a deposition, an interview through glass. Do not mismatch shoulder size on the reverse, and do not call a clean single an OTS.

Compared with similar shots

A Two-Shot gives both faces authorship. A Single removes the foreground partner; a dirty single may chew the edge without a true shoulder anchor.

A Reaction Shot may be taken as OTS or as a single. OTS means: near body fragment, far face subject.

Match the pair.

Two-ShotThe relationship is the shot.

SingleIsolate. The other person is gone even if they are in the room.

Extreme Close-UpA detail is the scene: an eye, a mouth, a trigger.

In film

The Social Network runs confrontations and depositions in this geometry. Heat's diner uses shared geography and opposing coverage between the two-shot and the tighter work.

The Silence of the Lambs interviews live on whose shoulder, whose glass, whose face. The Stendhal Syndrome connects a person and a painting through alternating views, related grammar of looking past one thing at another.

Grammar: relation still in the foreground.

The Social Network 2010Confrontational conversations and deposition coverage.

Heat 1995The diner exchange uses shared geography and opposing coverage.

Heat 1995The diner conversation between Hanna and McCauley.

The Silence of the Lambs 1991Clarice and Lecter’s interviews.

The Stendhal Syndrome 1996Anna and the painting are connected through alternating views.

Prompt it

Name the near shoulder and the far face. Example: Over-the-shoulder framing of [Subject], near shoulder soft in foreground, the far face sharp, looking toward the near shoulder, 180-line held.

Specify which body is near. For a pair, generate a matched reverse on the same side of the axis, same table and key.

Do not put both full faces to camera, and do not let the far person look into the lens.

Use in Video Generator

Generate two matching over-the-shoulder shots of a tense café conversation. A: the man’s blurred shoulder frames the woman’s face. B: her blurred shoulder frames his face. Preserve seat positions, cup placement and light direction. Edit on changing reactions, not every spoken word.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Two-Shot (both faces complete) or a Single (no shoulder). The tell is two people equally sharp, or a clean portrait.

The worse tell is a broken 180: the far person looks into the lens or away from the near shoulder, so the reverse would make them appear to sit on the same side. Fix: one soft shoulder, one sharp face looking at that shoulder, matched reverse, line held.

Questions

What is Over-the-Shoulder Coverage in film?

Over-the-shoulder coverage frames the far person as the subject while a near shoulder or head anchors the foreground. Paired OTS shots keep two people in a shared geometry even when we are close on one face.

Over-the-Shoulder Coverage vs Single

A single is one principal with no partner owning the foreground. OTS keeps a near shoulder or head in frame as a spatial glue. If the other person is gone from the rectangle, you have a single, even if they are still in the room.

When should I use Over-the-Shoulder Coverage?

Use it for dialogue that should keep the relationship physically present. Do not use it when isolation is the point, and do not mismatch the reverse.

How do I prompt Over-the-Shoulder Coverage for AI image or video?

Write Over-the-shoulder framing of [Subject], near shoulder soft in foreground, the far face sharp, looking toward the near shoulder. Name who is near. Hold the 180. For video, generate a matched reverse as a second shot on the same side of the line, rather than spinning the camera around them.

Does an over-the-shoulder shot break the 180-degree rule?

No. A correct OTS is how you hold the 180. The camera stays on one side of the line between the two people. The far face looks toward the near shoulder, not into the lens. Crossing that line flips screen direction and is a coverage error, not a look.
